title: Per-cohort TTL Bakeout and Quantization Scheduling (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This memo captures an experiment-first proposal for reducing token-level cost while preserving latency SLAs by combining per-user-cohort KV-cache TTLs with a scheduled quantization roll-forward. The central idea is to treat cohorts as independent signal sources for caching utility and to stagger quantization aggressiveness by cohort maturity, workload shape, and SLA. This is not a final playbook — it is a bakeout plan with measured checkpoints and spreadsheet-driven decision gates.

Why a cohort approach?
- Observed heterogeneity: our telemetry shows clear differences in average prompt length, repeat-prefix probability, and tail latency across customer cohorts (e.g., customer-managed chatbots vs. single-shot summarizers). A single TTL/quant config wastes cache value on ephemeral cohorts and over-provisions precision where it's not needed.
- Risk containment: incremental rollout by cohort reduces blast radius for quality regressions introduced by lower-precision quantization.
- Cost granularity: cohort-specific settings produce measurable cost deltas in the cost model spreadsheet and make it easier to credit savings to business units.

Definitions used in this doc
- Cohort: logical grouping of requests by stable attributes (customer-org, route, or interaction-class). We expect 6–12 active cohorts for most customers; the spreadsheet template assumes up to 20.
- TTL Bakeout: a short, time-boxed experiment where TTL values are swept per cohort to identify sweet spots for caching hit-rate vs. cache-memory cost.
- Quantization Schedule: phased application of qconfig (e.g., fp16 -> int8 -> int4) for a cohort, subject to quality checks.

High-level proposal
1) Instrument: add cohort labels to telemetry and extend the cost-model sheet with cohort_id as a primary key. Columns: cohort_id, example_routes, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_completion_tokens, prefix_repeat_rate, 95p_latency_ms, tail_loss_rate, current_ttl_s, candidate_ttl_s, batch_target_tokens, qconfig_candidate, est_cost_change_pct, quality_delta_est, rollout_stage.
2) Bakeout sweep (2 weeks): run TTL values [0s, 8s, 30s, 120s, 600s] for each cohort, track hit-rate, p95 latency, and per-token cost. Each cohort runs TTL values in isolated time windows (e.g., 8-hour windows) to reduce confounding.
3) Quant schedule (4–6 weeks parallel cadence): for cohorts that meet hit-rate and quality thresholds, apply conservative quantization (int8 static) during off-peak for 48–72h, evaluate on automated eval prompts and production signal (prompt-embedding cosine drift, BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy metrics for structured outputs). If no regressions, consider int4 mixed per-token quant for latency-insensitive cohorts.
4) Combine: when a cohort exhibits both high cache hit-rate (>= 18% improvement vs. baseline) and tolerable quality delta (<0.6% drift on evals), lock in TTL and move to the next quant stage.

Detailed experiment plan and spreadsheet columns (sample)
- cohort_id (string)
- owner_contact (string)
- sample_routes (short list)
- baseline_avg_tokens (number)
- baseline_p95_ms (number)
- baseline_cost_per_k (number)
- ttl_candidate_s (list)
- observed_hit_rate (number)
- delta_cost_per_k_pct (number)
- eval_quality_delta_pct (number)
- rollback_trigger (string)
- notes (string)

Example bakeout guardrails
- Minimum sample size: 50k tokens per TTL window per cohort before drawing conclusions.
- Latency SLO guardrail: any TTL or quant stage that increases cohort p95 latency > +12% or absolute p95 > SLA threshold must be reverted immediately.
- Quality guardrail: eval-quality-delta > 1.5% -> immediate rollback. For structured outputs, human-in-the-loop review required if automated proxy exceeds 0.7% drift.

Quantization schedule suggestions (conservative -> aggressive)
- Stage 0 (baseline): fp16 / kernel-optimized kernels.
- Stage 1 (safest quant): static int8 activation quant, 8-bit weight storage (expected cost delta: -12% to -18%). Run for 72h in off-peak, monitor evals.
- Stage 2 (mixed): mixed-int8/int4 with per-layer fallback for first N layers (expected additional delta: -6% to -10%). Apply only if eval drift < 0.4% over 72h.
- Stage 3 (aggressive): int4 + 2-bit AdaQuant fallback for large attention matrices on tail-agnostic cohorts (expected additional delta: -5% to -9% but higher risk). Requires canary and extended manual review.

Batching/throughput knobs (cohort-aware)
- Per-cohort target batch_tokens: derive from avg prompt tokens and target latency SLO. Start with small-batch SLO budgets: 1–3 token-targeted microbatches for <50ms SLOs, moving to 8–16 token batches for 200–400ms SLOs.
- Adaptive batch ceiling: set per-cohort max_batch_tokens to 2x observed avg tokens to avoid overbuffering.
- Priority routing: if cohort is SLO-sensitive, prefer low-latency routing nodes and disable cross-cohort batching to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Rollout gates and metrics to capture (collected per-cohort)
- cost_per_1k_tokens (before/after)
- cache_hit_rate (prefix + kv)
- p50/p95/p99 latency_ms
- eval_quality_delta_pct (automated proxies)
- customer_error_rate and rare-behavior-drift flags
- memory_used_per_instance_mb (to check cluster fit)

Spreadsheet-driven decision gates (example rule text)
- If cache_hit_rate increase -> est_cost_change_pct >= 6% AND eval_quality_delta_pct <= 0.6% -> promote TTL and schedule int8.
- If eval_quality_delta_pct > 1.5% at any quant stage -> rollback quant and mark cohort for manual review.
- If p95 latency increases > 12% -> rollback both quant and batching change for that cohort; mark as latency-sensitive.

Edge cases and heuristics
- Cold-start-heavy cohorts: if repeat_prefix_rate < 6% and session_length avg < 3 messages, set TTL=0 by default. Quantization is low-value here; focus on batching/packing to reduce cost.
- Conversational agents with long KV chains: use longer TTL (>= 300s) and conservative quant (int8 only) because prefix cache miss is expensive.
- Mixed-route cohorts: break out by route when pattern metrics diverge by >25% to reduce noise.

Logging and observability additions needed
- Cohort label in token-level traces and in KV cache logs.
- TTL-change event logging with before/after hit rates per window.
- Quant-stage annotations in model serving traces so we can correlate quality drift to kernel levels.

Runbook for rollbacks and stakeholder comms
- Automatic rollback: service should automatically revert to last-known-good config for that cohort if any guardrail trips.
- Human escalation: on rollback due to quality, notify owner+SRE+applied-ml with a summary (cohort, change, key metrics) and create a GitHub issue with reproducer prompts.
- Customer communication: if cohort belongs to a paying customer and rollback affects >5% of their latency or quality, send templated note with timeline and committed remediation steps.

Next steps (action items)
- Instrument cohort labels and extend cost-model spreadsheet. (owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-07)
- Kick off TTL bakeout on 4 pilot cohorts with diverse shapes (customer search, support-chat, summarization, internal-tool). (owner: Ethan; due: 2026-03-14)
- Add quant stage annotations to model traces and wire automated eval hooks. (owner: Maya; due: 2026-03-21)
- Prepare dashboard tile for cohort-level heatmap (hit-rate, est savings, p95) and add to Redwood Console drafts. (owner: Omar; due: 2026-03-28)

Open questions
- Should cohorts be defined at customer-org granularity or route-level by default? My recommendation: start org-level, split by route when TTL/metrics diverge.
- How often should we re-evaluate TTLs? Quarterly re-check is the default, but high-volatility cohorts should be re-evaluated monthly.

Appendix: quick spreadsheet formulas (examples)
- est_cost_change_pct = (baseline_cost_per_k - observed_cost_per_k) / baseline_cost_per_k * 100
- observed_cost_per_k = ((1 - hit_rate) * token_compute_cost + hit_rate * token_cache_cost) * 1000
- hit_rate = cached_tokens_served / total_tokens_requested

Final note
This proposal is intentionally conservative on quant aggressiveness and prescriptive on bakeout methodology. The goal is a repeatable, observable pathway from TTL experimentation to safe quant adoption with clear cost attribution per cohort. Looking for feedback on the spreadsheet column set and rollback thresholds before we spin up the pilot.
